note: Player opinions from the community codex, not game rules or guide data.
source: Buriedbornes 2 Codex, Notes column of the Origin, Race and Job tables. Wording paraphrased; tier = rating implied by the note.

Commoner.s: Praised as one of the best; extra dungeon events help with farming mod points, soulstones and sub-dungeons.
Commoner.t: Widely regarded as one of the best origins in the game. Players value its extra dungeon events for farming, since they can bring more mod points, soulstones and sub-dungeons.

Political Strife.s: Rated even higher than Commoner; its −50% EXP penalty is seen as minor, especially later on.
Political Strife.t: Rated even higher than Commoner by comparison. Players consider its −50% EXP penalty barely worth worrying about, especially later on, and call it an amazing origin.

Exile.s: Rated extremely good once you learn to manage remaining skill uses; awkward for 0-Shield builds.
Exile.t: Rated extremely good by players who learn to manage their remaining skill uses. The one drawback commonly raised is for builds that want 0 Shield.

Solitude.s: A free reset of skill remainings and HP stacks; losing minions is seen as no real cost.
Solitude.t: Seen as a free reset of skill remainings and HP stacks. Players say being unable to summon minions is no real downside for most people.

Loyalty.s: Pretty good: lets you craft skills and runes earlier, and losing mod points may not matter for some builds.
Loyalty.t: Considered pretty good. Players see it as a way to craft skills and runes earlier, and note that losing mod points may not matter, since some builds benefit less from the Mod Board.

Pacifist.s: A safe option with a small soulstone bonus; makes Savage mode harder to reach.
Pacifist.t: Described as a safe option: players note that +1 soulstone is not much, but that it brings some safety. The only downside they raise is that it makes entering Savage mode harder. One contributor recommends pairing it with the Traveler job and Human race for a safe run with lots of money.

Noble.s: The 100 soulstones are seen as small; considered good for speedrunning.
Noble.t: Players consider the 100 starting soulstones not much, and see the origin as good for speedrunning.

Ruination.s: Suited to short, quick runs where fast levelling matters; not recommended for long runs.
Ruination.t: Players say the level cap of 80 limits you less than it sounds: you end with less HP and fewer basic parameters, but the most important stats can still be maxed. Not recommended for long runs; seen as a fit for short, quick runs where fast levelling matters.

Rebel.s: Somewhat good for score farming, though one contributor finds it meaningless once Savage mode is reached.
Rebel.t: Described as somewhat good for score farming, and said to have been better in the past. One contributor avoids it because it mainly helps you reach Savage mode, after which the ability stops being useful.

Fugitive.s: Works like a teleport on escape; tricky, but usable for chest farming, ideally with events and Treasure Hunter.
Fugitive.t: Players describe it as essentially a teleport when you escape battle. With a smoke bomb it is seen as workable for avoiding fights, and although it can be tricky to pull off, it can be used for farming chests. One contributor recommends aiming for events and using Treasure Hunter.

Avenger.s: Average overall; the rune reroll bonus can make low-rarity runes harder to find.
Avenger.t: Rated average overall. The rune reroll bonus can make it harder to find the low-rarity runes you may want; players say this can matter but depends on the situation.

Vanity.s: Average overall; low-rarity equipment is rarely a problem unless you want open crafting slots.
Vanity.t: Also rated average overall. Unlike Avenger, players see no real downside to low-rarity equipment, except when you want open slots to craft in, where a remove-parts contract can help.

Believer.s: Seen as outclassed by the more consistent Exile.
Believer.t: Considered outclassed by Exile. Players call Exile more consistent, since resetting uses cannot take you above the maximum while Exile can.

Wanderer.s: Hardly worth taking, though its discount stacks with other crafting cost reductions.
Wanderer.t: Considered hardly worth taking, although its crafting discount can be stacked with other crafting cost reductions.

Occluded.s: Weak; Commoner or Political Strife are preferred for mod points.
Occluded.t: Considered weak. Players prefer Commoner or Political Strife for mod points, since events can provide them without needing to camp, and camps appear less and less often.

Barren.s: Rated poorly, and one contributor calls it terrible; Commoner or Political Strife are suggested instead.
Barren.t: Rated poorly; one contributor calls it terrible. Players say it combines downsides similar to Pauper's and Cunning's for a mediocre reward, and suggest Commoner or Political Strife instead, since events can supply mod points.

Pauper.s: Strongly discouraged; crafting is seen as too powerful to disable.
Pauper.t: Strongly discouraged. Players regard crafting as too powerful to disable in exchange for a benefit that crafting can already provide.

Succesful.s: Not worth it; 10 mod points is seen as too small a reward.
Succesful.t: Considered not worth it; players feel that 10 extra mod points is too small a reward.

Cunning.s: A poor trade-off, since higher rarity does not mean higher quality.
Cunning.t: Considered a poor trade-off, since players point out that higher rarity does not mean higher quality.

Human.s: Handy for handling debuffs such as Insanity; March Out helps you escape, restore HP or use Limit Releaser, and…
Human.t: Handy for handling debuffs such as Insanity; March Out helps you escape, restore HP or use Limit Releaser, and pairing it with Traveler can bring in many more soulstones.

Elf.t: Called a great race overall. Players warn that people get hooked on Genius without realising runes are much stronger. A good pick for an Evasion build or when you have just started.

Halfling.s: Praised as good for almost anything with nothing bad to say.
Halfling.t: Praised as good for almost anything with nothing bad to say. Scouting is very useful if you know how to use it, and its Cooldown and Consumption bonuses suit builds like Swordmaster.

Lizardman.s: Seen as newbie friendly thanks to its escape and HP restoration.
Lizardman.t: Seen as newbie friendly thanks to its escape and HP restoration. Sound Sleep is mostly useless but cleanses long Insanity; Robust and Tail Attack are praised.

Dragoon.s: A good race with solid bulk, unlocked very early.
Dragoon.t: A good race with solid bulk, unlocked very early. Samurai's Sheathing and Victory Cry help the first skill burst. Players say Golem is usually the better choice if it weren't for Victory Cry.

Fairy.s: Spirit Form is the main draw.
Fairy.t: Spirit Form is the main draw. Being stuck at 0 HP stacks without reliable resistance is risky, and players suggest giving it HP rather than Shield because of Spirit Form.

Dark Elf.t: Called newbie friendly. Pickpocket alt can give accuracy, Steady +100% is seen as nearly a must and comes free, and its ability restores Remaining Uses with multi-hit skills using Blind and Invert.

Vampire.s: A niche race the codex author loves.
Vampire.t: A niche race the codex author loves. Strong synergy with Old Doctor and Saint, a little with Death Knight, and it works best when you avoid origins that give Shield.

Wererabbit.s: Said to have the best ability in the game, but it is so squishy that players suggest using a Wererabbit head part on…
Wererabbit.t: Said to have the best ability in the game, but it is so squishy that players suggest using a Wererabbit head part on another race instead.

Angel.s: The codex author calls it one of the worst races, behind only Dog and Pumpkin.
Angel.t: The codex author calls it one of the worst races, behind only Dog and Pumpkin. Dignity and Brilliance make direct damage awkward, and its niche is limited to a few builds such as Purifier, Pirate or MaxHP-based damage.

Automaton.s: Not seen as attractive unless used with a werewolf head part.
Automaton.t: Not seen as attractive unless used with a werewolf head part. Overheat is fine, but similar results come from other sources without its downsides.

Lycanthrope.t: Reported as barely used. Players only want the Werewolf passive, which is available as a Lab Part, so the race itself mostly skips building mutation via Mask of Mutation and gets Willpower.

Pumpkin.t: Does nothing significant. Its multi-burst can be replicated, and Steady Effort plus one Free Skill gets you 4 bravery for the first burst anyway.

Giant.s: Warned as risky for newbies: Immortality is dangerous and you must manage steady and remaining protection.
Giant.t: Warned as risky for newbies: Immortality is dangerous and you must manage steady and remaining protection. The 8 HP stacks sound attractive but are unnecessary. Giant works better as a Lab Part for HP or Shield damage builds.

Outer One.t: Strong when used correctly. Majestic and especially Steel Body counter its excess Insanity, and it suits Insanity-boosted skills or Zealot. It also has 2 HP stacks and Willpower.

Dog.s: Called bad even after its update.
Dog.t: Called bad even after its update. Mostly something completionists will want.

Demon.s: Needs a lot of investment to match a standard race or job with equipment.
Demon.t: Needs a lot of investment to match a standard race or job with equipment. Eternal Youth and Resist: Large Damage +95% are near musts, and Wererabbit with Butcher's Machete helps with stats.

Ghost.t: Overshadowed by Infested. Not locked to 0 HP stacks like Fairy and has better resistance, but lacks HP and its ability is rarely useful. Grudge pairs well with Pirate.

Caterpillar.s: Works extremely well with HP or Shield damage skills; Magical Formation and Military's Cooperation can cap most…
Caterpillar.t: Works extremely well with HP or Shield damage skills; Magical Formation and Military's Cooperation can cap most resistances while raising damage. Good for consistent bursts without Valor.

Amorphous.s: Mostly valued for its head part on Demon and as a Valkyrie pairing because of its random stats.
Amorphous.t: Mostly valued for its head part on Demon and as a Valkyrie pairing because of its random stats. Fragile and odd, but players may favour it if dungeons keep getting shorter and harder, since mod points would grow faster.

Bone.s: Strong survival: duplicate Bone Graft with Auto: Life and Steady 100%, and with Steel Body almost nothing kills you.
Bone.t: Strong survival: duplicate Bone Graft with Auto: Life and Steady 100%, and with Steel Body almost nothing kills you. Foot Soldier gives a pseudo Exile and Valkyrie brings 5 HP stacks of toughness.

Zashiki-warashi.t: Rated kinda mid. Limited to its own job, but Invitation Fortune can be very good and it has abilities for its own survival. Its racial ability is weak for farming, though Wererabbit with Butcher's Machete can reset items every camp.

Merman.s: A good ability but no real function or niche, since Discipline can do the same job.
Merman.t: A good ability but no real function or niche, since Discipline can do the same job.

Golem.s: Called awesome: like Dragoon with built-in Steel Body and Plating plus extra power.
Golem.t: Called awesome: like Dragoon with built-in Steel Body and Plating plus extra power. 0 HP stacks don't stop you gaining them elsewhere, and it pairs with Spirit Form and Healthy or Defiant resistance. Restart is harder to build around but makes The Brilliance of Fraus very strong.

Medusa.s: Players want the Thrill ability, which with Foot Soldier activates twice and is great for farming keystones and Lab…
Medusa.t: Players want the Thrill ability, which with Foot Soldier activates twice and is great for farming keystones and Lab Parts. As a race it mainly suits Earth's Bind, though Crystalline Body enemies nullify petrification.

Infested.t: The codex author's favourite generalist. Mask of Mutation can give 200% Mutation or Machine Body (50% Ironclad, Sanctuary, Mutation plus restored remaining uses), and Magical Formation with Military's Cooperation adds resistances and damage.

Hive.s: With Steel Body its skill is a strong floor-long evasion and ailment resistance buff with no downside, and spamming…
Hive.t: With Steel Body its skill is a strong floor-long evasion and ailment resistance buff with no downside, and spamming escape recovers HP stacks quickly. The author pairs it with Disperse and Flame Torch's burst.

Twilight.s: Said to pair well with Zealot, but you need Willpower early and almost have to take Remaining Protection, Eternal…
Twilight.t: Said to pair well with Zealot, but you need Willpower early and almost have to take Remaining Protection, Eternal Youth or Crystalline Body, which limits head, leg and contract options.

Tengu.t: Wishes it had HP stacks. Its skill has a poor ailment hit, though Everchanging or Fluency make it a good debuffer. The author likes it with Knight plus Cheating, which skips worrying about evasion and ailment resistance.

Warrior.s: The +50% power for low-accuracy skills sounds fine but needs an accuracy source you could spend elsewhere, so it is…
Warrior.t: The +50% power for low-accuracy skills sounds fine but needs an accuracy source you could spend elsewhere, so it is rated kinda mid.

Cleric.s: Has Willpower so it can't be bad, but is called the worst of its group: it does little beyond healing and Divine…
Cleric.t: Has Willpower so it can't be bad, but is called the worst of its group: it does little beyond healing and Divine Punishment is lacking.

Ranger.s: Has a surprising synergy with Giant, and a Metal rune can make it shine.
Ranger.t: Has a surprising synergy with Giant, and a Metal rune can make it shine.

Wizard.t: The starting INT class. Focus is much stronger than before, and nearly doubling its value on 3 indirect magical damage sources makes scaling soar.

Foot Soldier.s: A very niche ability that can make Replenishment on Move rival Exile so skills are ready every room, but you may…
Foot Soldier.t: A very niche ability that can make Replenishment on Move rival Exile so skills are ready every room, but you may prefer something with more power.

Samurai.s: Mostly turns 2 hits of 70% into 3 hits, though direct hits have other benefits.
Samurai.t: Mostly turns 2 hits of 70% into 3 hits, though direct hits have other benefits. Milling and Pursuit are the go-tos, and it is oddly better with Magical Damage builds.

Viking.s: A good ability and it starts with Charge Up.
Viking.t: A good ability and it starts with Charge Up. Nothing special, but a Viking head or divine charm is still worth taking.

Vagrant.s: Told to just use a Free Skill instead: you don't need that much bravery, and it adds risk of sitting at 0 HP stacks.
Vagrant.t: Told to just use a Free Skill instead: you don't need that much bravery, and it adds risk of sitting at 0 HP stacks. Its niche is First Aid for Solven.

Spellblade.s: Looks cool on paper, but the best Enhancement sources already buff both physical and magical, so it adds little.
Spellblade.t: Looks cool on paper, but the best Enhancement sources already buff both physical and magical, so it adds little.

Executioner.s: Called dead: multi-hit skills have low crit rates and enemies resist crits, so you would need huge crit chance.
Executioner.t: Called dead: multi-hit skills have low crit rates and enemies resist crits, so you would need huge crit chance. Negative Resistance removes HP stacks better and raises damage.

Dark Knight.t: Strongly advised against. Avoiding all resistance on mod board and equipment and needing vulnerability on yourself is seen as not worth +30% penetration. Don't forget Steel Body.

Death Knight.s: Blood Armor and Dreadnought are seen as too much.
Death Knight.t: Blood Armor and Dreadnought are seen as too much. People use it with Fairy but waste 3 abilities on Blood Armor, and sitting at 0 HP stacks is risky.

Pirate.s: Its ability is called absolutely great, and Additional Hex, Explosion and Frostbite also trigger it.
Pirate.t: Its ability is called absolutely great, and Additional Hex, Explosion and Frostbite also trigger it. It pairs somewhat well with Ghost through Grudge.

Paladin.s: The enhanced damage is barely noticeable, but Retribution is almost a must for Reflect Damage builds.
Paladin.t: The enhanced damage is barely noticeable, but Retribution is almost a must for Reflect Damage builds.

Valkyrie.s: Doubles the power of about 90% of skills and lets them scale off your highest stat, which is called great.
Valkyrie.t: Doubles the power of about 90% of skills and lets them scale off your highest stat, which is called great. Players advise against pairing it with Angel just for Heaven's Spear, since Vampire does that better.

Dark Priest.s: The chance is so low it rarely does anything; one of the most obsolete jobs in the game.
Dark Priest.t: The chance is so low it rarely does anything; one of the most obsolete jobs in the game.

Zealot.s: Not called one of the best because a 5★ item gives Fear and its passive, but Fear is an advantage if used well.
Zealot.t: Not called one of the best because a 5★ item gives Fear and its passive, but Fear is an advantage if used well. With Outer One it gives lots of Prayer and damage, and with Ghost Jewel Crown and Moonshadow it becomes a void beast.

Ninja.s: Can't lower skills you just used enough to reuse them.
Ninja.t: Can't lower skills you just used enough to reuse them. Only great for skills with high cooldowns and mostly no Free Skill.

Scavenger.s: A solid ability, particularly when you capture monsters.
Scavenger.t: A solid ability, particularly when you capture monsters. Item Rarity +1 helps with rare drops and Item Reuse is simple to exploit, yet the job feels modest overall.

Thief.s: Called absolutely the worst job: Minimal Movement isn't worth it and may even get you killed.
Thief.t: Called absolutely the worst job: Minimal Movement isn't worth it and may even get you killed.

Bard.s: A mid ability (25% per unique buff, capped).
Bard.t: A mid ability (25% per unique buff, capped). Its Skill Rarity +1 stat also stops you rolling Charge Up, which would otherwise be great for it.

Torturer.s: Strong utility: Influence powers up Corruption and cuts indirect damage taken.
Torturer.t: Strong utility: Influence powers up Corruption and cuts indirect damage taken. Its payoff depends on knowing what the enemy will do.

Necromancer.s: The ability is useless but Command and Minion Transfer compensate.
Necromancer.t: The ability is useless but Command and Minion Transfer compensate. Summoning itself isn't great.

Traveler.s: Weak and forgettable unless used correctly, but then soulstones mean more power and it can be great early on.
Traveler.t: Weak and forgettable unless used correctly, but then soulstones mean more power and it can be great early on. The author wrote a guide for it.

Monk.t: Willpower is very valuable. Remember Hold can lock skills in alt mode. It is not great with Vampire, Automaton or Caterpillar because switching their skills to Alt Mode unprepared can be terrible.

Authority.s: Doesn't do much; the ability is quite useless.
Authority.t: Doesn't do much; the ability is quite useless. Dignity cuts direct damage dealt and taken, so Indirect Damage suits it better.

Druid.s: Used to be the author's favourite but is a weird niche: Influence +100% per debuff works for Influence-enhanced…
Druid.t: Used to be the author's favourite but is a weird niche: Influence +100% per debuff works for Influence-enhanced skills, but Purifier is the real DoT job.

Saint.s: Many ways to abuse it, very good especially with Vampire (inflict yourself with debuffs to kill enemies or heal a…
Saint.t: Many ways to abuse it, very good especially with Vampire (inflict yourself with debuffs to kill enemies or heal a lot while dealing HP or heal-based damage). Excessive Defense is praised.

Ancientmancer.s: Spirit Form raises HP, which raises Shield much more, improving survivability and damage.
Ancientmancer.t: Spirit Form raises HP, which raises Shield much more, improving survivability and damage. Shield reset still works with Apnea.

Taoist.s: Goes kinda hard early: starts with Tornado, which can't miss, and Concentration, whose burst gives double…
Taoist.t: Goes kinda hard early: starts with Tornado, which can't miss, and Concentration, whose burst gives double penetration to deplete HP stacks. Skill Rarity +1 stops you finding Energy Bolts, though.

Witch.s: Ignoring enemy magical resistance is very good.
Witch.t: Ignoring enemy magical resistance is very good. Ancient Shield is unreliable since you can't restore it if lost before combat, and max shield means nothing in PvP.

Old Doctor.s: Medical Practice alt burst can deal a lot of damage and it is hella fun to play.
Old Doctor.t: Medical Practice alt burst can deal a lot of damage and it is hella fun to play. Called a perfect combination with Vampire.

Swordmaster.s: Not the strongest but a cool niche; mostly relevant when enemies inflict Exhaust, and may not suffice against high…
Swordmaster.t: Not the strongest but a cool niche; mostly relevant when enemies inflict Exhaust, and may not suffice against high Risk and Difficulty.

Scholar.s: The power increase isn't great, but many skills have under 100 power and hit many times, so you get stronger buffs…
Scholar.t: The power increase isn't great, but many skills have under 100 power and hit many times, so you get stronger buffs and debuffs.

Knight.t: Tanky. Cheating makes you use your rightmost skill, likely before enemy Preemptive Use skills and Auto: Combat. Lance Charge is a great skill.

Miner.s: A meme job with only extra soulstone gain.
Miner.t: A meme job with only extra soulstone gain. Probably decent for speedrunning with Ruination, but otherwise not good for much.

Priest.s: Doesn't seem to have a reason to exist: most players already handle Skill Consumption, and Delay Heal is a niche…
Priest.t: Doesn't seem to have a reason to exist: most players already handle Skill Consumption, and Delay Heal is a niche skill that is only 4★.

Engineer.s: Good if you're later in the game; pairs with Wererabbit passive and an elixir for strong plays.
Engineer.t: Good if you're later in the game; pairs with Wererabbit passive and an elixir for strong plays. Heavy Attack means you shouldn't hit yourself.

Witch Doctor.s: The codex author says they're the only one who uses it, since under 50 total remainings is usually bad.
Witch Doctor.t: The codex author says they're the only one who uses it, since under 50 total remainings is usually bad. It does go well with Local Procurement and Infested.

Shrine Maiden.s: A fun concept but bad as a strong later-game option.
Shrine Maiden.t: A fun concept but bad as a strong later-game option. You are locked to few skills or lack Willpower to Invert skills and resist debuffs, and then the job doesn't function.

Purifier.s: Called stupidly strong: its damage lands after a skill and is boosted by your buffs, so extra Burn doubles value…
Purifier.t: Called stupidly strong: its damage lands after a skill and is boosted by your buffs, so extra Burn doubles value from Magical Enhancement. It gave Additional Bleed/Burn/Poison a use and made DoT a good option.

Hunter.s: A newer job described as what Executioner wishes it could do: guaranteed accuracy and crit, skill lock from the…
Hunter.t: A newer job described as what Executioner wishes it could do: guaranteed accuracy and crit, skill lock from the start and more indirect damage.

Eccentricity.s: Huge HP and stacking skill power, with the downside of always needing Pure Hit and Willpower.
Eccentricity.t: Huge HP and stacking skill power, with the downside of always needing Pure Hit and Willpower. Skeletal Adjustment can give it Willpower, so Metal Bones go best on it.

Jester.s: Skill power can't be bad, but unlike Zealot its buff lasts only one room, and Drunkyard gets far more power from a…
Jester.t: Skill power can't be bad, but unlike Zealot its buff lasts only one room, and Drunkyard gets far more power from a 25% Drunkenness skill than Jester gets from 10% trick.

Sage.s: A free Skill Boost +100%, fine with Exile at 200+ remaining, and pairs with Heavy Steps Blueprint for 80% Boost…
Sage.t: A free Skill Boost +100%, fine with Exile at 200+ remaining, and pairs with Heavy Steps Blueprint for 80% Boost Proficiency. Generally good, but nothing significant.

Pugilist.s: Players expected a pseudo Auto: Turn with Ultimate in Martial Arts, but skills must be put back on Default mode to…
Pugilist.t: Players expected a pseudo Auto: Turn with Ultimate in Martial Arts, but skills must be put back on Default mode to reuse. Called bad.

Sand Swordsman.s: Seen as the Spellblade fix players wanted: more value from Charge Up, a way to remove HP stacks, and Sand Storm gets…
Sand Swordsman.t: Seen as the Spellblade fix players wanted: more value from Charge Up, a way to remove HP stacks, and Sand Storm gets Magical Enhancement while dealing Physical damage.

Hermit.s: Players rank it at the very bottom, below even Priest.
Hermit.t: Players rank it at the very bottom, below even Priest.

Dog.s: Only usable by the Dog race.
Dog.t: Only usable by the Dog race.

Demon.s: Evil Researcher combos very well with Wind Shield.
Demon.t: Evil Researcher combos very well with Wind Shield. Only usable by the Demon race.

Zashiki-warashi.s: Restricted to its matching race, yet Cage of the Soul makes it a decent choice.
Zashiki-warashi.t: Restricted to its matching race, yet Cage of the Soul makes it a decent choice.

Hive.s: Limited to its own race, but it starts with 9 HP stacks, a skill giving a lot of evasion and ailment resistance, and…
Hive.t: Limited to its own race, but it starts with 9 HP stacks, a skill giving a lot of evasion and ailment resistance, and a way to recover HP stacks, which is called quite insane.

general: The guide does not rank origins. In the community codex, players most often place **Commoner** and **Political Strife** at the top. Commoner is praised as one of the best origins in the game because its extra dungeon events help with farming mod points, soulstones and sub-dungeons, and Political Strife is called even better, with its −50% EXP penalty seen as minor, especially later on.

**Exile**, **Solitude**, **Loyalty** and **Pacifist** are also well regarded, while **Noble**, **Ruination**, **Rebel**, **Fugitive**, **Avenger**, **Vanity** and **Believer** are seen as mixed or situational.
At the other end, **Barren**, **Occluded**, **Pauper**, **Cunning**, **Wanderer** and **Succesful** are rated poorly, with Barren called terrible.
beginner: The guide does not rank origins, and the codex does not name a beginner pick, so this draws on its overall ratings. Players most often praise **Commoner** as one of the best origins in the game, because its extra dungeon events help with farming mod points, soulstones and sub-dungeons. **Political Strife** is rated even higher, with its −50% EXP penalty seen as minor, especially later on, and **Pacifist** is described as a safe option, though it makes Savage mode harder to reach.

Players rate **Barren** poorly, describing a mediocre reward bundled with downsides like those of Pauper and Cunning, and suggest Commoner or Political Strife instead. **Occluded** draws the same advice.
Origin.poor_lead: In the community codex, players rate these origins poorly. For Barren and Occluded they point to Commoner or Political Strife instead.
Origin.poor_extra: **Believer** is not rated poorly outright, but players see it as outclassed by Exile.
